title: Hackers breach US Air Force Cloud One military platform
seoTitle: US Air Force Cloud One breached by hackers
dek: Unidentified hackers breached the US Air Force's Cloud One computing platform, according to media reports. The Pentagon declined to confirm or deny the intrusion while maintaining its systems are secure.
happened: On 27 November 2026, media outlets reported that hackers breached Cloud One, the US Air Force's primary cloud computing platform. According to Reuters, the intrusion was uncovered during a system upgrade when attackers exploited a software vulnerability to gain access to the control system. The Air Force subsequently paused planned platform migrations, blocked updates to running applications, and revoked certain administrator permissions. Investigators contacted US Cyber Command to evaluate the incident. Cloud One integrates infrastructure from Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Oracle, supporting critical functions such as logistics, aircraft maintenance, personnel records, ammunition tracking across more than 200 locations, and North American air defense radar integration. It remains unconfirmed whether classified data or sensitive military information was stolen. In response to inquiries, the US Department of Defense declined to confirm or deny the breach, citing operational security policy, while maintaining that military systems remain safe and operational.

sides.says: Asserted that its systems remain safe and managed continuously, while declining to address network intrusion reports due to security policies. Official statements noted that "systems are safe, secure, and managed 24/7 by the best experts and teams in the world."
Declined to comment on network security or operational status, stating it "does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems."

next: US Cyber Command will continue evaluating potential data exposure while system updates and back-office migrations remain paused.
summary: Hackers breached the US Air Force's Cloud One computing platform, according to reports published on 27 November 2026. The platform hosts critical operational applications, including weapons inventory tracking at over 200 sites and air defense radar integration. The intrusion was discovered during a system upgrade. The Air Force suspended updates and involved US Cyber Command, while the Pentagon declined to confirm the breach, maintaining its systems are secure.
